title: A connection starts before the first message.
intro: A new visitor arrives at Talkie with a choice: who do I want to talk to? After choosing a character, the challenge changes—finding a way into the conversation and feeling part of its world.

As the sole Product Designer, I owned the Web redesign and subsequent feature design. The work connected two goals: helping people find a suitable character on arrival, and deepening immersion and emotional connection once they started chatting.

blocks.label: DESIGN QUESTION
blocks.text: How might we help someone choose a character, enter their world, and make the conversation their own?

items.label: FIND
items.title: Give people a starting point.
body: Help visitors explore through character cues, interests and scenarios—even when they do not have a name to search for.

items.label: ENTER
items.title: Keep the conversation in focus.
body: Make character context accessible while giving the exchange itself a clear visual center.

items.label: PARTICIPATE
items.title: Leave room for the user.
body: Support what to say, who to be, and how to continue without taking the final choice away from the person chatting.

The redesign established the shared navigation and visual structure. Subsequent features extended that foundation through discovery, reply assistance, persona settings and ways to revisit conversations.
